open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Data-provider enumerations and row models (2026-11-08)
open_points.text: a key that is not yet an enumeration becomes one
open_points.question: Are CapabilitySet, ImportAuditReason, TransportGuardRefusal and BootstrapCommandOutcome release-defined value types minted by SPEC_STANDARD from the data provider, or are their members runtime outcomes minted by the product actions that return them?
options: They are canonical release values minted by SPEC_STANDARD from the data-provider closure.
They are runtime values minted independently by the authorization, import, transport-guard and bootstrap actions.
The type definitions are release-minted, but each occurrence is a distinct runtime fact.
open_points.default_guess: Treat every member as a canonical release-defined value emitted from the data provider.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Data-provider enumerations and row models (2026-11-08)
open_points.question: Are the data-provider tables normative inputs that determine authorization, permitted status changes, audit classification, HTTP responses and command outcomes, or are they only non-behavioural descriptions of decisions made elsewhere?
options: The tables are normative and generated code must behave according to them.
The tables merely describe behaviour fixed elsewhere and cannot determine it.
Only some tables are behavioural, but the text must identify which ones.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the tables as normative because generated code reads them.

witness.initial: A capability exists in the taxonomy, and a CapabilitySetMember row can say whether an operator set contains it.
events: An operator invokes an action guarded by that capability.
The authorization implementation consults, or declines to consult, the data-provider table.
outcomes: The row controls whether the action is authorized.
The table cannot change behaviour, so authorization is determined by some unstated source.
witness.observer: The operator invoking the protected action

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M40 — CapabilitySetMember
open_points.text: whether a CapabilitySet holds a Capability
open_points.question: Must CAPABILITY_SET_MEMBERS contain exactly one row for every CapabilitySet–Capability pair, or may it contain only selected pairs; if a pair has no row, is membership false or unspecified?
options: A total matrix contains one true-or-false row for every pair.
Only member=true pairs are present and absence means false.
Rows may be sparse and absence means the capability-set fact is unspecified.
open_points.default_guess: Require a total matrix with exactly one row per CapabilitySet–Capability pair.

witness.initial: A capability set and capability are both valid closed-taxonomy members, but their pair has no row.
events: A principal using that capability set invokes an action requiring the capability.
outcomes: The missing pair is treated as member=false and access is refused.
The missing pair is treated as an incomplete specification rather than a false membership fact.
witness.observer: The requesting principal and the deployment operator

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M41 — StaffStatusTransition
open_points.text: whether a staff status may change to another
open_points.question: Must STAFF_STATUS_TRANSITIONS contain exactly one row for every ordered StaffStatus pair, or may disallowed transitions be omitted; what fact does an absent pair represent?
options: Every ordered pair has one row whose allowed field supplies the fact.
Only allowed transitions are present and absence means disallowed.
Absence means the transition has not been specified and must not be interpreted as false.
open_points.default_guess: Require one row for every ordered status pair.

witness.initial: A staff account is in a valid status and the requested destination is valid, but the pair has no transition row.
events: An administrator requests the status change.
The status-change action looks up the pair.
outcomes: The absent pair means allowed=false, so the change is refused normally.
The absent pair exposes an incomplete model rather than a decided refusal.
witness.observer: The administrator and the affected staff member

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M42 — PrincipalStatusTransition
open_points.text: whether a principal status may change to another
open_points.question: Which of the three deliberately separate principal types does PrincipalStatusTransition govern: ServicePrincipal only, ClientViewer and ServicePrincipal, or all principals including StaffAccount?
options: It governs ServicePrincipal status only; StaffAccount uses M41 and ClientViewer revocation is separate.
It governs every non-staff principal, including ClientViewer and ServicePrincipal.
It is a common transition model for all principal types, with M41 as an additional staff-specific view.
open_points.default_guess: Apply it only to ServicePrincipal because staff has M41 and the product says the three principal types are never merged.

witness.initial: A ClientViewer is active and an administrator revokes the viewer.
events: The administrator performs the viewer-revocation action.
The implementation decides whether to validate the change through PRINCIPAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS.
outcomes: The viewer is a principal governed by M42, so the transition must exist and be allowed there.
M42 governs ServicePrincipal only, so viewer revocation does not read it.
witness.observer: The administrator and the revoked viewer

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M42 — PrincipalStatusTransition
open_points.text: whether a principal status may change to another
open_points.question: For the principal type or types M42 governs, must PRINCIPAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS contain one row for every ordered status pair, or does omission itself mean disallowed?
options: It is a total matrix with one allowed value per ordered pair.
It lists only allowed transitions and omission means disallowed.
It may be sparse, and omission means the transition fact is unspecified.
open_points.default_guess: Require a total matrix with one row per ordered status pair.

witness.initial: Both principal statuses exist, but their ordered pair has no row.
events: An administrator requests the status change.
outcomes: The missing pair is a decided disallowed transition.
The missing pair is a missing model fact that cannot be treated as a refusal.
witness.observer: The administrator and the affected principal

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M43 — SupportedContractVersion
open_points.text: Read only as rows of the constant SUPPORTED_SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT_VERSIONS and SUPPORTED_OCR_CONTRACT_VERSIONS
open_points.question: Is a supported version identified only by its integer, as the stated value identity implies, or by the pair of contract family and integer so that equal snapshot and OCR version numbers remain different facts?
options: The integer alone identifies the value, and the same value may be shared by both constants.
Identity is contract family plus integer, requiring a contract-family field or distinct row types.
The rows have integer identity only within their owning constant, although that context is not a field.
open_points.default_guess: Add contract family to the identity so snapshot version 1 and OCR version 1 are distinct support facts.

witness.initial: Snapshot contract version 1 and OCR contract version 1 are both supported.
events: The release emits a version:1 row in SUPPORTED_SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT_VERSIONS.
The release emits a version:1 row in SUPPORTED_OCR_CONTRACT_VERSIONS.
outcomes: The equal fields make them the same M43 fact shared by two constants.
The owning constants make them two distinct support facts for different external contracts.
witness.observer: Generated validators and a maintainer changing support for only one contract family

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M45 — TransportGuardStatus
open_points.text: TransportGuardRefusal — closed enum: untrusted_host | allowed_preflight | unlisted_preflight_origin | logout_origin_mismatch | oversized_body | rate_limited, the responses the transport guard produces
open_points.question: Is allowed_preflight actually a refusal with a refusal status, or is TransportGuardRefusal misnamed and intended to include successful transport-guard outcomes?
options: allowed_preflight is a successful outcome, so the enum and M45 cover more than refusals.
allowed_preflight is nevertheless a refusal, and the text must state what is being refused.
allowed_preflight does not belong in TransportGuardRefusal or TRANSPORT_GUARD_STATUSES.
open_points.default_guess: Treat allowed_preflight as a successful guard outcome and rename the enum/model concept to cover guard outcomes rather than refusals.

witness.initial: A browser sends a preflight request from a configured allowed origin.
events: The transport guard classifies the request as allowed_preflight.
The HTTP layer reads TRANSPORT_GUARD_STATUSES for that classification.
outcomes: The classification is a successful preflight response.
Because the value is a TransportGuardRefusal and M45 supplies the status of a refusal, the request receives a refusal response.
witness.observer: The browser making the cross-origin request
